To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
actor-oriented tools have been useful in promoting pro-poor interventions.
actor-oriented approaches can help NGOs and donors to identify and strengthen key local actors and partnerships.

the use of actor-oriented tools has helped to: (i) identify the key people, partnerships and networks in the project area; (ii) understand their role and contribution; (iii) identify constraints and opportunities; (iv) identify and prioritise interventions that are appropriate to the context; and (v) monitor and evaluate project activities in a participatory manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to build a more effective and sustainable development approach that works with and through people and partnerships.

the following question: how can we develop a methodology for identifying, analysing, and building partnerships that are sensitive to the needs of the poorest people in the context of the political economy of development?
understanding the role of social networks and social capital in the process of economic development and poverty reduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the actor-oriented tools were useful in identifying the key actors, networks, and partnerships, and that the approach was a useful tool in helping to identify the most appropriate interventions to target the poorest.
the use of actor-oriented tools in this NGO context helped to promote pro-poor partnerships, and to build the capacity of local actors.

this approach is a useful way of thinking about development interventions, and is a useful tool in the hands of a reflective practitioner, but it is not a ‘magic bullet’ that can be easily applied in any context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strong nets catch fish.
strong networks catch fish, and strong nets catch more fish.
we are now much better at identifying and working with local partners, and at identifying and addressing the constraints faced by the poorest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the poorest people are often the most excluded, and the most marginalised, from local development networks.
strong nets catch fish.
strong local actors are essential in building pro-poor partnerships.
